title: Hollerhorn Distilling Grappa
about: Hollerhorn Distilling sits on a hillside outside Naples, the old grape village at the south end of Canandaigua Lake. Karl Neubauer, a Naples native and longtime custom home builder, studied distilling for some fifteen years before he and his wife Melissa opened in 2018, in a building Karl framed from timber salvaged out of collapsing barns. A fire in May 2022 destroyed the tasting room, but the stills and barrels survived, and the couple rebuilt with help from the whole valley. Karl works almost entirely with fruit and grain grown within a short drive of the distillery.

Grappa is a pomace brandy: rather than distilling wine, the distiller ferments and distills what is left after the grapes are pressed, the skins, seeds and pulp that still hold much of the fruit’s aroma. Hollerhorn’s is made from the Riesling pomace of McGregor Vineyard on Keuka Lake, one of the Finger Lakes’ pioneering Riesling growers, so the region’s signature grape carries straight through into the spirit.

Most grappa is bottled clear. Hollerhorn rests this one in small barrels made for the distillery from New York white oak and New York black cherry wood, toasted rather than charred so the wood adds a gentle sweetness without heavy smoke or color. Hollerhorn describes ripe Riesling, burnt orange, cherrywood and hibiscus over a subtle toasted oak note, with an aromatic, almost perfumed lift. Try it after dinner, neat.
facts: Riesling pomace from McGregor Vineyard, Keuka Lake
Toasted New York white oak and black cherry barrels
